messages.subject: changes to algorithms
parts:
This is in response to the proposed change to NUTS
(if you count adaptation, I thin this makes it NUTS-III).

I think Michael should have the final decision on how the
HMC algorithms work.

I personally like this proposed change.

How are we going to test these things? I don't want to
run into another logjam, but I'd like to know that you at
least ran this on a few models and it wasn't terrible in
performance.

It'd be nice to make these tests part of our integration
testing --- I saw that there was at least one test for
logistic regression in place that at least reported on speed
of something.

- Bob

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] changes to algorithms
parts:
> I don't want to
> run into another logjam, but I'd like to know that you at
> least ran this on a few models and it wasn't terrible in
> performance.

Yes, I did tests on a few models to ensure that the adaptation
still worked and I was able to recover the true expectations
within the standard error. I also made a note for any reviewer
to do the same in the PR.

> It'd be nice to make these tests part of our integration
> testing --- I saw that there was at least one test for
> logistic regression in place that at least reported on speed
> of something.

There is one test that looks at speed and the final sample,
which is stochastic and _not_ a good test for reasonable
MCMC output. In particular, even if the changes are valid
the test will fail and have to be updated.

I did have tests prototyped that would actually check for
posterior coverage, but they can’t be run within Stan itself
due to our lack of proper API routes. This was yet another
reason for a refactor but, well, we all know how that went.
